lessons.title: я (ya) — the word for I, written small
lessons.gloss: ya — the word for I, written small

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, for letter shapes on the page
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, for letter shapes on the page. You can listen to everything else now — leave the sections called Script you'll notice: я and Guided Practice until you have stopped, and I will say so again when we reach it.

segments.text: Before the new one: write й and ю once each, and name them.
Now say я (ya), "I". You have read it for a long time. This lesson takes one letter out of it and puts it in your hand.

я (ya) is also a whole word: "I". You wrote the capital Я in the letter chapters, but Russian writes "I" with the small letter: inside a sentence it is never capitalised, unlike English "I". So this is the shape you will write most.
1. start here: climb the right stem from the baseline to the top.
2. without lifting, curve counterclockwise around the upper bowl.
3. without lifting, sweep left through the bowl's lower join.
4. without lifting, descend the diagonal leg to the lower-left tip — and only now lift.
Pen lifts: 0. The pen never leaves the paper.

Stroke order is one attested teaching order; hands and teachers vary. Source: RussianIrina, ‘Learning Russian - Alphabet letters, handwriting’, lowercase я (ya) demonstration, 12:13–12:21, YouTube, 5 February 2013.

segments.instruction: at я (ya) and point at я (ya) inside it
segments.source: [YOU LOOK: at **я** and point at я inside it]

segments.instruction: я three times, saying ya as you finish each one
segments.source: [YOU TRACE: я three times, saying *ya* as you finish each one]
[YOU WRITE: ю, then я, from memory]

segments.text: Which letter is this — я? (ya, ya.) Which word did it come from? (я, ya, "I".)
